From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Ranking published by Forbes magazine
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Forbes_logo.svg/250px-Forbes_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Forbes_logo.svg)Logo of _Forbes_ magazine [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Angela_Merkel_2019_cropped.jpg/250px-Angela_Merkel_2019_cropped.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Angela_Merkel_2019_cropped.jpg)[Angela Merkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Merkel "Angela Merkel") has been ranked the most powerful woman 14 times.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_list_of_the_World's_100_Most_Powerful_Women#cite_note-MerkelStreakof4-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_list_of_the_World's_100_Most_Powerful_Women#cite_note-MerkalStreakof10-2)
Since 2004, _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_ , an American business magazine, has published an annual list of its ranking of the 100 most powerful women in the world. Edited by prominent _Forbes_ journalists, including [Moira Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moira_Forbes "Moira Forbes"), the list is compiled using various criteria such as visibility and economic impact. In 2025, the gauge was "where do women hold real power".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_list_of_the_World's_100_Most_Powerful_Women#cite_note-forbes2024-3) The top 10 per year are listed below.
